newsitem.title: USA: FALCONBRIDGE ADJUSTS TO ONTARIO STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: FALCONBRIDGE ADJUSTS TO ONTARIO STRIKE.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd is adjusting the flow of nickel matte into its Kristiansand refinery in Norway to compensate for a strike at its Sudbury, Ontario, operations and will avoid going to the spot market to meet its obligations, a company executive told Reuters Wednesday.
John Smillie, Falconbridge's director of marketing, declined to specify the economic or operational impact the strike was having on the company's nickel business.

"The situation is very fluid," Smillie said. "We keep working the numbers for different scenarios -- two weeks, one month, six months. We want to try to make whatever matte we have last the duration of the strike."

Falconbridge has some Sudbury matte stockpiled, though Smillie declined to say how much. The refinery also treats matte from BCL Ltd's Phikwe smelter in Botswanna, which is expected to produce 25,000 tonnes of contained nickel this year.
The Kristiansand smelter produced 70,000 tons of refined nickel in 1996.
"Certainly if there's an opportunity in the spot market, we're going to take it, but we'd rather make whatever we have last a little longer before we consider that option," Smillie said.
Sudbury produced 45,700 tonnes of nickel, 50,000 tonnes of copper and 1,600 tonnes of cobalt including custom feed, last year.
The copper market has given the strike a ho-hum, with a portion of the copper matte processed at its Kidd Creek complex in northern Ontario and the remainder shipped to Kristiansand.
"We're not concerned about copper," Smillie said.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
